messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Automatic SEV2: spike in TLS handshake failures and 5xxs for hosted API in us-east-1 (paths to /v1/chat). Pager to @carmen (primary) and @derek (backup).

carmen: I'm oncall and seeing client reports of TLS alert handshake failure + repeated `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Pulling gateway logs now. Will start timeline.

infra-bot: Detected anomaly at 2026-03-12T02:12:24Z. Error rate for /v1/chat up from 0.8% -> 22% in 3m. Affected subnets: 10.101.0.0/16, 10.102.0.0/16.

derek: I have NLB metrics 1:11 UTC shows surge in TCP RST and 524s. Also seeing DNS SERVFAIL for our api-redwood.* records from some resolvers. Could be two separate failures colliding.

oya: starting packet captures on edge nodes edge-a/edge-b. Running `sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/tls-3.pcap tcp port 443` and grabbing `journalctl -u envoy -n 400`.

net-eng: checking VPC peering and TGW state. Noted a route propagation event at 01:58 UTC where a new transit attachment was created and withdrawn due to a config drift. Some route tables in us-east-1 remained with stale path to an older NAT fleet.

carmen: grabbing cert inventory across CDN, ALB, and internal proxies. Use `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.test -showcerts` against a sample of impacted IPs.

oya: pcap shows frequent `ICMP type 3 code 4` (fragmentation needed) during TLS handshake. Also many retransmits before server sends Certificate. On a few streams I see `TLS alert: handshake_failure` right after the client finishes ClientHello. Sample tcpdump excerpt:```
15:12:25.123456 IP 198.51.100.45.52340 > 10.10.1.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
15:12:25.123899 IP 10.10.1.12.443 > 198.51.100.45.52340: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
... then ICMP frag needed with mtu 1400 ... then retransmit ... then TLS alert handshake_failure
```

derek: that strongly points to PMTU/MTU issues. But why `x509: unknown authority`? Could be unrelated partial cert rollout. Carmen, what do certificates show?

carmen: pulled cert fingerprints: some edge nodes present CA chain with fingerprint SHA256:AA:AA:... (old intermediate removed last week), others present SHA256:BB:BB:... (current). Couple of internal proxies are serving a chain missing intermediate CA leading to validation failures on upstream checks. Ill paste the list to the incident Gist.

infra-bot: cert-rotation-job ran at 2026-03-11T03:05Z. Logs show `cert-writer` succeeded on 90% of hosts; 10% returned `EACCES` when writing to /etc/ssl/redwood.pem. Retry explainer: job retried three times and then marked succeeded by controller despite per-host failures (bug in job status aggregation).

net-eng: interesting: the route drift caused some traffic to flow through older NAT hosts that still had the old AMI. That AMI includes iptables drop rules blocking ICMP type 3 by default (legacy firewall rule). So a path had MTU mismatch and ICMP blocked -> PMTU blackhole -> TCP streams stalled -> TLS handshake fails. At the same time the old NAT path also terminated TLS to an upstream proxy that lacked the rotated intermediate CA, causing `unknown authority` for some connections. Two independent failures combined to create larger impact.

oya: can we try MSS clamp as a quick mitigation and re-enable ICMP?

net-eng: applying MSS clamp on affected NATs and enabling ICMP frag-needed acceptance on the transit path. Will roll to canary (2 NATs) first. Command: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` on canary NATs.

support-bot: Notifying CS triage: top impacted customers flagged: FluxDrive, PaperTrail, and CloudNote. Sending interim message template.

derek: while net-eng deploys clamp, I'm going to tag and re-run cert-rotation for nodes that failed. We should avoid a blind retry; patch the permission bug first. What changed permissions?

carmen: I dug into AMI changes: an AMI upgrade introduced a systemd tmpfile config that made /etc/ssl/redwood.pem owned by `sslmgr:sslmgr` instead of `root:root` during image bake; cert-writer runs as rootless service and couldn't overwrite. Patch candidate: run cert-writer as root or revert tmpfile mode. Creating infra ticket now.

net-eng: MSS clamp canary applied at 02:16Z. Monitoring: canary error rate fell 21% -> 3% within 70s. Good signal MTU blackhole was primary immediate cause. Rolling clamp to remaining NATs in us-east-1.

oya: re-running tcpdump after clamp shows fewer retransmits and successful three-way TLS exchanges. Still seeing occasional `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` from certain proxies. Those are likely the nodes that never got the updated chain.

infra-bot: action list created: 1) net-eng to normalize MTU and re-enable PMTU ICMPs permanently; 2) infra to fix cert-writer permission and re-run rotation only after verifying FS ownership; 3) add post-rotation end-to-end TLS healthcheck; 4) add alert for IP_FRAG_FAILED or ICMP frag-needed counters.

derek: I patched cert-writer to temporarily escalate to root for the write step and re-ran rotation on the three failed nodes (proxy-17, proxy-19, proxy-24). They now show new fingerprint SHA256:BB:BB:... and validation tests pass. I'll open a follow-up to design a least-privilege fix.

carmen: rolling mitigation looks effective. Error rates dropped cluster-wide from 22% -> 4% in 10 minutes. Customer updates sent. Support reports that FluxDrive's traffic normalized after 2 minutes.

security: do not enable any permanent TLS fail-open. The cert fix must be validated with cryptographic fingerprints and chain verification. We'll do a key-rotation audit post-incident.

net-eng: long-term plans: enforce MTU at AMI level, add bootstrap script to set ENI MTU to 9000 on startup, and add TGW route sanity checks to detect mixed-MTU paths. Also we will update our maintainers to allow ICMP type 3 messages for PMTU.

oya: compiling timeline for RCA: 01:58Z transit attachment created (config drift) -> 03:05Z partial cert-rotation (permission failures on ~10% hosts) -> 02:12Z anomaly detector fires (TLS failures spike) -> 02:16Z MSS clamp canary -> 02:18Z region-wide clamp -> 02:25Z cert re-sync completed on failed hosts -> 02:40Z errors back to baseline. Will add pcaps and cert fingerprint map to the postmortem.

carmen: on-call handoff: I'll hold until infra ticket INF-6789 (perm fix) merged and net-eng confirms MTU normalization. If stable, hand to oya at 08:00 UTC.

infra-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated, severity lowered to SEV3. Postmortem required. Attach artifacts to INF-6789 and SEC-1302.

support-bot: Sent final customer follow-up with summary and ETA for permanent fixes. No escalations reported.

carmen: thanks team. Great cross-discipline coordination. I'll draft the RCA and include mitigation artifacts, timeline, and action owners. Closing thread but will append links to the postmortem doc here when ready. :white_check_mark:
